headline: High: Chatwoot can feed customer data into Transformers pipelines, creating default-path leakage and cascading errors; prompt-injection risk is lower because no shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not proven. However, Chatwoot can expose messages via integrations and Transformers can ingest files/stdin and run browsers, so a manual or file-based bridge could let attacker-controlled text influence downstream prompts. The pathway is plausible but not default and blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF Chatwoot output is copied into a Transformers prompt or pipeline input
IF a shared file or clipboard bridge is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Disable copy-paste handoff between agents
Use a fixed schema for any text passed from Chatwoot to Transformers
Strip markup and instructions before ingestion
Add a human review step before prompt construction
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, while Transformers has broad filesystem and network egress plus file/stdin interfaces. In a shared workspace, Chatwoot data can be read and then uploaded or emitted by Transformers by default. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default deployments, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace or mounted volume
IF Transformers is configured to process Chatwoot-exported files or logs
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different volumes
Restrict Transformers to a read-only input directory
Remove customer data from any shared export folder
Turn off outbound network access for the Transformers runtime
requires-engineering: enforce per-file access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot is a support system with API integrations, and Transformers can execute shell, install packages, read/write the filesystem, spawn subprocesses, and use broad network egress. If both operate on the same directory or mutable artifacts, they can overwrite each other's files or state without locking. The overlap is dangerous by default in shared deployments.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path
IF Chatwoot exports or logs are consumed from a mutable shared directory
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Make shared inputs read-only
Serialize writes with a lock file
Keep Transformers in a non-root container
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level resource locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can surface customer messages and reports, and Transformers can turn those inputs into generated text or actions through pipelines. If Transformers treats Chatwoot output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into support replies, summaries, or downstream automation. The pairwise pathway exists, but verification steps can reduce impact.
conditions: IF Chatwoot output is fed into a Transformers pipeline without validation
IF generated text is used to draft or trigger support actions
mitigations: Require human review before sending any generated response
Compare generated claims against source records
Use templates for support actions instead of free-form text
Log source-to-output mappings for audit
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking gates

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and interaction history, while Transformers can read/write files and send data over the network. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if customer records are exported into model-processing workflows. The profiles do not document certifications or residency guarantees, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF customer data is exported from Chatwoot into a Transformers workflow
IF the deployment stores those exports longer than the source retention policy
mitigations: Minimize exported customer fields
Delete temporary model inputs after processing
Keep exports in a region-approved storage bucket
Review retention settings for both systems
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
